notes:
This was a resume run, but nothing had been left behind: src/atlas/entries/ischemia.ts and other.ts did not exist, and there were no stray files from this workstream. I wrote both files from scratch, following the schema in src/atlas/schema.ts and the tone of the existing entries.

What was written:
- ischemia.ts has 21 entries. The 7 STEMI territories, rv-infarction, de-winter, wellens, avr-elevation-diffuse-std, hyperacute-t and sgarbossa-positive are critical, and each has an urgency statement. The others are st-depression-ischemic, t-inversion-ischemic, reciprocal-changes, pathological-q, old-mi-anterior, old-mi-inferior, old-mi-lateral and lv-aneurysm.
  - The entries use the occlusion-MI framing throughout. The ST-elevation thresholds come from the 4th UDMI by sex and age, written once as a shared criterion: V2–V3 ≥2 mm in men ≥40 y, ≥2.5 mm in men <40 y, ≥1.5 mm in women; ≥1 mm elsewhere.
  - V3R/V4R (≥0.5 mm, ≥1 mm in men <30 y) and V7–V9 (≥0.5 mm, ≥1 mm in men <40 y) have their own placement criteria.
  - Also covered: the posterior STEMI equivalent; de Winter; Wellens, including the advice not to stress-test; aVR elevation with diffuse ST depression framed as multivessel or left-main ischaemia, not as a STEMI; Sgarbossa, Smith (ST/S ≤ −0.25), Barcelona and paced rhythm (Dodd); the LV aneurysm T/QRS rule; UDMI Q-wave criteria, with Q waves tracking infarct size rather than transmurality; and the South African flag pattern.
  - There are no 'subendocardial / subepicardial ischaemia' labels; the entries describe the morphology instead.
- other.ts has 23 entries, with urgency statements for all 7 critical findings: hyperkalemia, hypothermia, pulmonary-embolism, brugada-type1, na-channel-blockade, pacing-failure-capture and pacing-oversensing.
  - Hyperkalaemia: the progression sequence, poor correlation between the ECG and serum K, and that any ECG change is an emergency.
  - Pulmonary embolism: sinus tachycardia is the commonest finding; S1Q3T3 is explicitly called insensitive and nonspecific; the ECG can neither confirm nor exclude PE.
  - Brugada: only type 1 is diagnostic; a drug-induced type 1 needs supporting features; type 2 is suggestive only, with the β angle.
  - Also covered: ARVC (Task Force 2010 and Padua 2020); HCM, apical HCM and takotsubo; TCA toxicity (QRS 100/160 ms, aVR rules, bicarbonate); the athlete international criteria; and pacing malfunctions, including the magnet response of a pacemaker vs an ICD.
- I reconciled every criterion with docs/curriculum/criteria.md and critic.json. Every criterion source resolves to a full reference. Spanish uses Spain terms (derivación, aurícula, IAMCEST, SCASEST, ICP primaria) and decimal commas.

After the advisor review I made these changes:
- I removed the speculative 'stemi-evolution' scenario preference from hyperacute-t and pathological-q. It would have shown a chip labelled with a different finding.
- I dropped the de Winter aVR number. Sources disagree on it, so the entry now says only 'slight ST elevation in aVR'.
- I re-attributed the HCM Q-wave definition to Elliott 2014 (ESC HCM).
- I removed one unused reference (Schröder 1994).

The lab already covers stemi-anterior, stemi-anteroseptal, stemi-inferior, stemi-lateral, stemi-posterior, reciprocal-changes, st-depression-ischemic, avr-elevation-diffuse-std, pathological-q, old-mi-inferior, hyperkalemia, hypokalemia, hypercalcemia, hypocalcemia, hypothermia, pericarditis, brugada-type1 and pulmonary-embolism.
